intent: Build a Slack bot that summarizes daily standup threads and posts a digest each morning.

blueprint_rows.name: Parse and summarize each standup thread
blueprint_rows.description: Read a day's standup thread per channel and produce a short structured summary.

effectiveness.reason: A wrong summary costs a human a re-read of the thread, moderate but not severe cost of error.

efficiency.reason: Runs once per channel per day, low volume, no human watching latency.

difficulty.reason: Bounded summarization over well-specified input/output, not open-ended reasoning.

pick.what_flips_it: If daily volume exceeds ~50 channels, drop to Haiku on a batch call to hold latency/cost.
pick.why_not_tier_above: Opus's extra reasoning depth isn't needed for a bounded single-thread summary.
pick.why_not_tier_below: Haiku's smaller context risks truncating a long thread before it's summarized.

blueprint_rows.rationale: Bounded, well-specified summarization; Sonnet at low effort clears the bar for a fraction of the default tier's cost.

blueprint_rows.name: Look up each channel's configured digest recipients
blueprint_rows.description: Resolve which users should receive a given channel's digest.
blueprint_rows.query_layer_note: Answered by a single indexed lookup against the workspace's channel-config table; route via a deterministic query layer instead of a model call.

effectiveness.reason: A wrong lookup just misroutes one message; cheap to catch and retry.

efficiency.reason: Runs once per channel per day, pure key-value lookup, no reasoning content.

difficulty.reason: Single indexed lookup against structured config, no ambiguity.

pick.what_flips_it: If recipient routing ever needs interpreting free-text preferences instead of a structured config row, promote to a model call.

blueprint_rows.rationale: Pure structured lookup; a query layer is reliable by construction and removes hallucination risk entirely, at less cost than even the cheapest model tier.

pick.what_flips_it: If daily volume exceeds ~50 channels, drop to Haiku on a batch call to hold latency/cost.

work_routing_map.rationale: Same reasoning as stage-1: bounded summarization, Sonnet at low effort.

assumptions: A channel-config table already exists and is queryable
would_measure: Actual per-channel summary token count once real thread lengths are known
Whether Haiku alone clears the bar once volume passes the stated flip condition

calibration.notes: No recommended-vs-actual calibration history available yet for this repo; reasoned from first principles.
